title: Facebook’s Oculus Rift Virtual Reality Headset Is Coming to Best Buy
summary: Facebook's Oculus Rift virtual reality headset will soon be available for demo and purchase at 48 Best Buy locations across the United States starting May 7th, with more stores to follow. This initiative aims to allow consumers to experience the VR headset firsthand, as Oculus works to fulfill existing pre-orders. Additionally, a limited number of Rifts will be sold online via Microsoft and Amazon.

title: Housewares Show brings out stylish, tech-savvy designs
summary: The Housewares Show in Chicago highlighted new product trends focusing on healthy eating, tech-savvy designs, and stylish aesthetics. Innovations include smart kitchen appliances, advanced cookware, and a continued emphasis on color and natural materials in home decor, reflecting consumer demand for convenience, health, and expression.

title: Amazon is about to overtake Macy’s as biggest seller of clothing in U.S.
summary: MarketWatch reports that Amazon is poised to surpass Macy's as the leading clothing retailer in the U.S. by 2017. This shift highlights the struggles of traditional retailers like Macy's and Kohl's in competing with e-commerce giants and adapting to consumers' online shopping habits. Analyst firm Cowen & Co. expressed increased confidence in Amazon's continued dominance in the apparel market.

title: Oracle Says It Considered Developing Its Own Phone Before Google Suit
summary: Oracle’s CEO Safra Catz testified in court that Google's distribution of Android for free significantly impacted Oracle's licensing revenue from Java, causing a "very negative impact" on payments from companies like Samsung and Amazon. Oracle claimed Google stole its copyrighted software for the smartphone market, leading to a lawsuit seeking $9 billion in damages. Catz also revealed that Oracle had considered developing its own phone but ultimately did not pursue the project.

title: ServiceNow Cloud Management adds Microsoft Azure support
summary: ServiceNow's Cloud Management suite now supports Microsoft Azure infrastructure, expanding its capabilities beyond Amazon Web Services and VMware. This integration offers a unified system for automating cloud management, providing templates for self-service requests, a single security model, and tools for managing total cost of ownership and compliance. The company plans to add support for more public cloud providers in the future.

title: Kroger's big $4 billion expansion plan
summary: Kroger plans a significant $4 billion expansion in 2016 to open new stores, renovate existing ones, and upgrade technology, critical for maintaining its market position against competitors. This investment includes substantial spending in the Cincinnati/Northern Kentucky/Dayton market and is aimed at increasing market share in existing regions, as highlighted by CEO Rodney McMullen. The strategy also includes expanding its ClickList service and continuing a "fill-in" approach by upgrading acquired subsidiaries.

title: Can Dick’s Sporting Goods hang on to its current lead over Amazon?
summary: MarketWatch examines whether Dick's Sporting Goods can maintain its competitive edge against Amazon in the sporting goods sector. Although Amazon is a major retailer, Credit Suisse and Boomerang Commerce analysis suggests that Dick's Sporting Goods currently holds a stronger position in this specific market compared to other retailers challenged by Amazon. Analysts anticipate a positive performance for Dick's Sporting Goods in 2017.

title: Debenhams Names Amazon Fashion’s Sergio Bucher as New Chief
summary: Debenhams Plc, the UK department-store chain, has appointed Sergio Bucher, Amazon Fashion Europe's vice president, as its new chief executive officer. Bucher, who has also worked at Puma and founded Inditex's Oysho lingerie brand, is set to join in October, succeeding Michael Sharp. Following the announcement, Debenhams' shares saw a rise of up to 2.6%.
